title: The Crusades, honestly
hookLine: armed pilgrimages that included massacres in Jerusalem and attacks on Jewish communities

lines: A CLOTH CROSS AT THE SHOULDER.
cards: A piece of cloth, cut in the shape of a cross, sewn onto a tunic at the shoulder.

In the accounts of that day, a pope has just finished preaching to a crowd in France, and people are pressing forward to vow that they'll go east. Farmers, knights, priests. Some will walk all the way to Jerusalem.
They think of themselves as pilgrims. They are also an army. The word crusade holds both of those at once, and today asks us not to drop either half.

teach.b: Pope Urban the Second urged Western Christians to go east, to help Christians there and to reach Jerusalem. The accounts that survive disagree about his exact words.
Those who answered took a vow and marked themselves with the cross. So a crusade was an armed pilgrimage: prayer and penance, joined to war.

Before they even left Europe, bands of crusaders turned on Jewish communities in towns along the Rhine. Jewish chronicles from those towns remember the dead, and families who chose death over forced baptism.
Some bishops sheltered Jewish families; some could not stop the killing.
When the crusaders took Jerusalem, they killed its people, Muslims and Jews, in the streets and in holy places. A Christian chronicler who was there describes the slaughter without shame.

There were voices from inside the Church too. When a monk later stirred up attacks on Jews during another crusade, Bernard of Clairvaux wrote that the Jews were not to be persecuted, and went in person to silence him.
And in a jubilee year, Pope John Paul the Second led the Church in asking God's forgiveness for violence used in the service of the truth, and for sins against the people of Israel.
Telling it honestly means keeping both halves: the faith that made people walk so far, and the crimes some of them committed on the way.

how: Catholics pray for peace in the Holy Land at Mass and in parish intentions, and the Church's own acts of repentance, like the Day of Pardon in the jubilee year, name the violence of the past alongside its faith.

games.q: you're a bishop in a Rhineland town. a band of crusaders arrives and threatens the Jewish families. what do you do?

games.why: some bishops sheltered Jewish families from the crusaders; in other towns the attempt failed, and the Jewish chronicles remember the dead.

practice: Hold the Holy Land in mind, its hills and old stone streets, and the people who live there now, of every faith, and those grieving there today, without taking a side.
If you pray, the Douay-Rheims psalm gives you the words: pray ye for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem. If you don't, hold them with a wish for their safety.

wordCard.voice: Crusade. An armed pilgrimage under the sign of the cross, joining prayer and penance to war, and carrying both faith and grave crimes. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: cross. those who vowed to go were said to take the cross, and wore one of cloth.
